newsitem.title: USA: Staples hearing set for May 19 in federal court.
newsitem.headline: Staples hearing set for May 19 in federal court.

text.p: A Federal District Court judge on Monday set a hearing for May 19 on the government's move to block a merger between office superstores Staples Inc. and Office Depot Inc. as anticompetitive.
Judge Thomas Hogan said each side would have two-and-one-half days to present witnesses and arguments to help him make his decision.

Hogan said he will decide within two weeks after June 5 -- when he will hear final oral arguments -- whether to grant the government's request for a preliminary injunction. That injunction would block the merger until all legal proceedings in the case were over.

The government argues that permitting the merger to create a combined 1,000-plus store chain would drive up prices by limiting competition. Staples and Office Depot argue that their merger would lead to lower prices.

Staples had sought a 10-day hearing with nearly two dozen witnesses to make its case, while the Federal Trade Commission had urged the judge to make his decision based solely on comprehensive written filings.

The government plans to hold an administrative law trial on the merits of the case if a preliminary injunction is issued. The FTC's chief litigator, George Cary, has said such an administrative trial would last 5 1/2 months.
But Donald Kempf, attorney for Staples and Office Depot, said if the government wins the preliminary injunction the case is virtually over.
Under an agreement between the government and the defendants many of the filings in the case are confidential and said to be proprietary.

The states of Maryland, New York and North Carolina filed a "friend of the court" brief asking that they be permitted to examine the confidential materials. The states are among those considering entering into the case.
Staples and Office Depot have opposed giving the states access to the materials.

Dow Jones Inc., publisher of the Wall Street Journal, filed papers with the court Monday seeking to open the files "to ensure the public's access to ... all pleadings and court documents filed in this matter."
Office Depot stock fell 37.5 cents to $13.625 on the New York Stock Exchange, while Staples was off 19 cents at $20.625 on Nasdaq.
